newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Top Argentine military officers to be retired.
newsitem.headline: Top Argentine military officers to be retired.

text.p: Argentina's Defence Minister announced on Thursday that three top military officers, including controversial naval chief Adm. Enrique Molina Pico, would be retired.

Minister Jorge Dominguez said President Carlos Menem had decided the head of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Mario Candido Diaz and Air Force chief Juan Paulik would also go at the end of the month, local news agencies reported. The reports cited no reason for Menem's decision.

Army chief Gen. Martin Balza, who last year made South American history by formally apologising for his force's human rights abuses during the "dirty war" against leftists in the 1970s, will stay in his post, Dominguez said.
Molina Pico was at the centre of a long-running diplomatic spat with France over his declarations in defence of one of Argentina's most notorious "dirty warriors", Capt. Alfredo Astiz.

Astiz, dubbed "the blond angel" by human rights groups, lives freely in Argentina but is wanted by Interpol for crimes including the kidnap and murder of French nuns Leonie Duquet and Alice Domon in 1977.

Molina Pico said last year that Astiz had "all the moral conditions to be a Navy officer". He also embarressed the government last week by publicly mentioning the possibility of a military conflict with neighbouring Chile -- once a bitter regional rival but now a major trade partner.

But Molina Pico and Paulik both followed Balza's cue last year and made public mea culpa's on behalf of their forces for their behaviour during the 1976-1983 rule of the juntas. Human rights groups believe up to 30,000 people died during the military's campaign against leftist guerrillas.

Dominguez said that Molina Pico would be replaced by the chief of the presidential guard, Carlos Marron. Molina Pico's current deputy, Jorge Enrico, will become the new head of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, and the Air Force will be headed by its operations commander, Ruben Montenegro.
